bottleneck: A candidate momentum effect may depend on market regime even after horizon robustness.
changed: Created deliverable: volatility-gated momentum evidence test
Established volatility gate as falsification test for momentum
complexity_added: Established new evidence artifact for future research
next: The evidence supports the existing alternating role framework and momentum research direction. The volatility gate approach is not productive for momentum, suggesting the need to explore alternative conditioning mechanisms or continue with the existing momentum research program.
objective: Test one explicitly predeclared past-only volatility gate on lookback-5 momentum through the existing regime-stability and null framework.
observed_effect: The past-only volatility gate (annualized vol < 0.20) eliminated the momentum edge, converting AMZN from REGIME_STABLE to CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE and JPM from REGIME_DEPENDENT to CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE, with all 10 assets showing no edge under the gate.
question: Does a single past-only volatility gate create a predeclared robustness improvement for the qualified momentum effect?
research_result: Negative conclusion: The past-only volatility gate (annualized vol < 20%) did not create a robustness improvement for lookback-5 momentum. Ungated momentum shows REGIME_STABLE (AMZN) and REGIME_DEPENDENT (JPM), while gated momentum shows CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE for all 10 assets. The volatility gate that was previously falsified for MA crossover also fails to help momentum.
uncertainty_reduced: Volatility gate conditioning does not provide robustness to momentum; in fact, it appears destructive, removing what would otherwise be positive momentum edges.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the same class of conditioning (past-only volatility gate) that was previously falsified for MA crossover would help momentum signals.
verified: Leakage discipline verified for both ungated and gated signals
